newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Illegal euthanasia widespread in Australia - survey.
newsitem.headline: Illegal euthanasia widespread in Australia - survey.

text.p: An estimated 37,000 euthanasia deaths occur each year in Australia as a result of doctors intentionally accelerating a patient's death, according to a confidential new survey of 3,000 Australian doctors.

The survey, published in the The Medical Journal of Australia, defined euthanasia as any death "intentionally accelerated by a doctor", which it said went beyond the contemporary narrow definition of euthanasia as a death caused by a drug administered at the patient's request.

Euthanasia is illegal in Australia except in the outback Northern Territory which introduced the world's first voluntary euthanasia law last September. Three people have used the law, which the Australian parliament threatens to overturn.
The study included deaths caused by a doctor withholding or withdrawing treatment in what it said was a "traditional definition" of euthanasia.
It found the rate of doctor-assisted death in Australia was double that of The Netherlands where voluntary euthanasia was practised.
The survey found that Australian doctors were far less likely to discuss their decision to hasten a patient's death with the patient or even seek their consent.

"The study shows that there are higher rates of non-voluntary euthanasia in a country with prohibitive laws than in a country that allows the open and regulated practice of voluntary euthanasia," said Dr Helga Kuhse, one of the authors of the study at Monash University in Victoria state.

"The lack of consultation between Australian doctors and patients is of special concern. Doctors may be reluctant to openly discuss end-of-life decisions with their patients in a situation where there is fear of prosecution."
Fellow author Dr Peter Singer said: "Our findings undermine suggestions that allowing euthanasia to be practised openly makes it more likely that doctors will end patients' lives without consent".

The survey was conducted by three doctors at Monash University. It was the first to study the actual number of medically-assisted deaths in the country. Doctors participated in the survey on condition that they remain anonymous.

The Australian parliament's House of Representatives, or lower house, late last year voted to overturn the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law and the upper house, or Senate, is due to vote in the next few months.
Opinion polls have shown overwhelming public support for voluntary euthanasia and doctors have said the practice does occur, unofficially, outside of the Northern Territory.
Australian euthanasia campaigners recently formed a group to push for nationwide laws allowing assisted suicide.
